statement: For every negative full once-punctured-torus outer involution, the full F-centralizer of its actual cusp reflection is trivial. Every cusp reflection has the same property, and the D58 fusion transporter g is unique. Every unit-multiplier transporter for either literal reflection v_i is exactly the specified single element c^((mu-1)/2)g or c^((mu+1)/2)g^-1. The one-section-class extension is real projective. The complete D61 conjugator problem reduces to the exact F-conjugacy c^-mu a_mu,i ~ a_mu,i with these unique elements and the original cusp retained.
depends_on: D58 actual negative extension, full cusp dihedral group, two local reflection classes and their exact F-fusion; D59 primitive full homology of the transporter and the other fixed-group homology map; D74 actual Delta/Hom duality, transpose transgressions, localized half-boundary rank, bar-prism coefficient transports and finite coset-module witness; C-WilkesRelativeAccepted2018 Propositions 5.7 and 6.16 for the completed once-punctured-torus pair; A-KochloukovaZalesskii2007 full finite-coefficient Brown theorem; D60 actual torsion quotient character; D61 exact boundary-generation test and standard extension maps; D62 full primitive centralizers, root coordinates and all-unit reflection labels; C-HaranArtinSchreier1993 Proposition 2.2
manuscript_passages: Section 30, folios 194-196, scans 383-387; Section 31, folios 198-199 verso, scans 391-394; Section 24, folio 147 verso, scan 293; Part D(b), full loop-outer finite actions in type (1,1)
depends_on_doubtful_reading: None. The actual one-cusp E/D coset module is identified with F/L by explicit inverse-topology and action maps. Its two local section occurrences are transported by the identity and the specified D58 g. Both lie in the cusp class; the other global normalizer factor, when present, maps to zero in boundary cohomology.
computational_checks: No computational claim. The actual one-cusp coefficient maps, both incidence transports, universal finite permutation witness, all-unit half-exponent identities and full root/extension coordinates are proved directly for the full groups. The already executed D58-D62 identities retain their original labels.
notes: The genus-one surface-pair duality uses its original single commutator boundary. It gives the same equality of high absolute and relative dimensions as D74 without assuming any transgression vanishes. Brown identifies boundary restriction with one duplicated restriction, forcing surjectivity and full fixed-group triviality. The two-class other fixed group remains characterized only by the previously proved normalizer, first cohomology and surjective fixed-line map. The unique transporter is homologically primitive; no free basis containing it is asserted. The exact remaining conjugacy and recognition problem is explicitly retained.
